cells.tense: Right now the fast read and the deep sense of what counts are moving together with the pen in hand.
cells.act: let yourself be drawn before you choose
cells.ask: Something keeps tugging at you with no case attached. Go toward it once — an afternoon, a conversation — and look, before deciding anything.
cells.core:
You can size up a situation quickly and still land right about what deserves your attention. The pattern arrives before the reasoning does, and you don't rush to justify it — that's what's working. People bring you the thing they can't sort out, and you're looking in the right place already. None of it needs defending to hold.

What this balance is free to feed next is a pull you haven't followed. Something has been drawing at you — a possibility, a direction, a feeling you keep setting down because there's no case for it yet. Let yourself be drawn before you choose. Go look at it up close. You don't have to commit, and you don't have to know why. Seeing it plainly is the whole of the act, and no one is asking you to file it anywhere.
cells.sheetLine: The pattern shows up in you before the reasoning does.
cells.verb: Cutting through what is said to the pattern underneath it
cells.place: Where what deserves attention is clear before the reasons for it are

cells.tense: A call you keep circling is still ahead of you, and the bracing has already started.
cells.act: decide it and act the same day, without explaining
cells.ask: Pick the thing you keep circling, settle it, and move that same day. No laying out reasons, no announcing first.
cells.core:
The read is right; the timing is off. Where you know what to attend to, you're seeing three moves ahead, and the reading is good enough that you keep refining it instead of using it. Every version left open is another future you don't have to walk into. What used to settle things has started producing more to settle.

The same depth is trying to become structure — a decision that holds because it doesn't argue. So pick the thing you've been circling and settle it, then move that same day. The structure does the work; the announcement doesn't. If you're wrong, you'll have a wrong answer instead of a good question, and you can move from there. You can't move from a question.
cells.sheetLine: What used to settle things now produces more to settle.

cells.tense: The moment asked you to know what counted, and you answered from a place you'd already left.
cells.act: cross over to the people it actually requires
cells.ask: Someone you've let drift — no falling out, just distance. Go be with them, not to fix anything.
cells.core:
Where you know what to attend to, the read is running on the last version you had. You answer from an old pattern, applied to what's here now, and people get a correct response from someone who isn't quite present. The analysis is still sharp. It's cutting things that aren't there.

Any way back runs through people, not through sharper attention. So pick someone you've let drift — no falling out, just distance — and go be with them, not to fix anything. Being near a person who knows you without the analysis returns you to what's actually here. Do the reading again afterward, when you're back.

cells.tense: You are reading the pattern right now and calling it something else while it works.
cells.act: follow the pull of what might be felt, a little way
cells.ask: Notice what draws you — a person, a direction, an hour you want back — and follow one pull a little way, without explaining it yet.
cells.core:
You're already seeing the shape of things before the evidence comes in — people bring you what they can't read, and your answer holds — and you'd say that's just how you think. It isn't. This has a source, and you've been filing it under circumstance, or luck, or simply how things are.

So let it show you something you didn't plan. Notice what draws you — toward a person, a direction, an hour you want back — and follow one pull a little way. Hold it as a possibility rather than a verdict. No explaining, no choosing yet. Following the pull is where it turns out to be yours, and staying with it plainly is the whole point.
cells.sheetLine: The reading is yours, and you filed it under circumstance.

attempts.check: Unsupported claim: that the person's reading of situations is fast enough to land on the first true thing under pressure — the record gives the mechanism (analysis broadcasting outward before it deepens) but not their speed, and I've written the Too Little cell as if I watched them. A reader could reasonably say they simply know what matters and don't need to slow down, and my read would be wrong about the mechanism, not just the degree. The asks survive that: each is one small act a camera could see, drawn from the medicine's own list, and none needs the person to agree with my reading to be tried. The sentence that serves me more than them is 'you've stopped checking' — it flatters the reader's eye and puts a verdict where an observation belongs.
